text:
Alex (runtime): heads up — getting an escalated ticket from a customer about huge p95/p99 spikes starting ~10:15 UTC after the canary deploy. They report tail latencies up 4-5x and many errors for heavy-chat routes. grabbing graphs now :eyes:

Alex (runtime): looking at traces, KV prefix cache miss rate jumped from ~2% to ~28% for model=gpt-omega-pref and route=/chat/stream. bundle of cold gets. here's the high-level metric: `cache.miss_rate{prefix=gpt-omega-pref,route=chat}` spikes at 0.28 at 10:12 and stays high for ~20m.

Maria (sre): thanks. any correlate with autoscaler events or pod churn? did dedicated pools resize?

Alex (runtime): weird — no pod restarts around then. autoscaler steady. but I do see a lot of KV eviction events. `kv.evictions{zone=us-west1}` goes up. eviction policy set to LRU for that pool.

Jon (oncall): I pulled one trace: https://internal-traces/trace/abc123 (paste). Key thing: each token generation call has full prefix-key lookup, but keys look different on subsequent turns. suspect cache key construction bug.

Sophie (eng-infra): can you paste an example key? if the key includes unique request id or per-request timestamp that's our cache thrash culprit.

Alex (runtime): example from logs (sanitized): `prefix_key=v1|model:gpt-omega-pref|route:chat|session_id:9f3a7c|input_hash:abcd1234`. notice `session_id` was recently added in a refactor to help observability — that's bad.

Maria (sre): yep that would make cache effectively per-session. :facepalm: That explains miss rate and eviction pressure. how many sessions are active?

Alex (runtime): customer is high concurrency, thousands of short sessions, so cache thrash. eviction exceeded the target working set.

Sophie (eng-infra): proposed fixes: 1) revert session_id in cache key asap (hotfix), 2) increase cache capacity as short-term mitigation, 3) add unit test to prevent request-scoped fields in cache key, 4) add histogram metric `cache.unique_key_cardinality` per minute.

Jon (oncall): for rollback: current commit is `deploy/2026-03-15-1008`. rollback to previous build `deploy/2026-03-15-0920` will remove the key change. I can trigger rollback if we agree.

Alex (runtime): also we can add a graceful fallback: if miss_rate > 0.2 then route to warm-cache fallback model (smaller KV footprint) to preserve latency SLOs. patch suggestion below: ```diff
- cache_key = f"v1|model:{model}|route:{route}|session_id:{sid}|input_hash:{h}"
+ cache_key = f"v1|model:{model}|route:{route}|input_hash:{h}"
```

Maria (sre): create an alert for `cache.miss_rate > 0.15 for 5m` and `kv.evictions > threshold`. add runbook steps: rollback, bump cache, enable fallback routing.

Sophie (eng-infra): I'll open a PR with the diff + unit test to assert deterministic keys (no ephemeral fields). tagging @alex for review.

Alex (runtime): repro steps for local QA: 1) run load generator `scripts/load-chat.sh --concurrency 300 --sessions-per-min 2000` 2) tail `kv.*` metrics 3) run two variants: with session_id vs without. you should see miss rate jump.

Jon (oncall): workaround for customer while we patch: enable sticky routing to route their sessions to dedicated pool with larger cache. also throttle session churn at the proxy (limit new sessions/sec) — they agreed to temp throttle.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15-1008 started by alex — status: success :white_check_mark:

Alex (runtime): timeline: patch PR in 15m, deploy hotfix canary in 30m, if no regression promote. if not possible roll back now. which is safer?

Sophie (eng-infra): hotfix small; but since it affects cache key logic I'd prefer rollback + patch merged, then deploy. rollback is fastest to reduce p99.

Maria (sre): agreed — rolling back now. Jon, can you coordinate with customer so we don't cause more churn?

Jon (oncall): on it. pinging customer support and enabling sticky routing + throttle. will post status updates.

Alex (runtime): follow-ups: - add telemetry to tag misses by codepath (compile vs runtime) - add eviction budget per-pool so we don't evict other tenants - schedule postmortem and add a checklist to PR reviews to check cache key surface area.

Sophie (eng-infra): PR: https://git.internal/pr/7823 (hotfix) — includes unit test and changelog entry.

Jon (oncall): rollback done at 10:40 UTC. p95/p99 back to baseline within 6m. customer confirmed. closing escalation after postmortem. :tada:

Alex (runtime): thanks everyone. lesson: never add ephemeral fields to cache keys without a feature gate + perf test.

Maria (sre): adding the runbook edits and alert. I'll file follow-up action items and assign owners.

Sophie (eng-infra): will open a small lint rule to flag `session_id`-like fields in cache key builders.

Alex (runtime): end.
